sounds.text: That road is mine. Keep moving.
One clean shot. Keep the car steady.
Close the distance. I will catch the rest.
Give me a gap. I will make it wider.
Hold still. This engine has one more run in it.
Road is clear. Keep your wheels under you.
Too much scrap in the way. I will shift it.
Clear path on the left. Follow my dust.
Outsiders don't find this road by accident. Come in, driver.
Turn around, driver. This road has a toll.

sounds.text: Kestrel One, this is Tremblant base. Welcome aboard. I will be on the radio the whole way, so take your time.
W and S raise and lower the collective. The arrow keys tilt her. A and D turn the nose.
Lesson one. Ease up on W and lift her three metres off the pad. Then hold her there.
That is it. Hold her steady.
Nice lift-off. You are a natural.
Lesson two. Keep her inside the circle, two to five metres up, for ten seconds.
You are drifting. Small touches on the arrows.
Rock steady. That is a real hover.
Lesson three. Bring her down on the H. Slow and gentle.
Smooth landing. The fuel pump and the dispatch board are yours now.
Lesson four. Hook the crate with H, carry it out to the circle, and set it down gently.
Watch the swing. Slow down and let the load settle.
Clean set-down. You are cleared to carry cars.
Not quite. Let us try that again.
No harm done. Go again when you are ready.
Kestrel One, you are low on fuel. Head for a pad.
Engine out! Lower the collective and glide. Pull up on W just before the ground.
Good landing. The fuel truck is on its way.
That was a hard landing. The mechanics will want a look at her.
Kestrel One, are you all right? We will fix her up and bring you home.
Easy! That one dropped hard.
Careful with the cargo, Kestrel One.
Job is on the board. Hook up and head out when you are ready.
Delivered. Nice flying, Kestrel One. The pay is in your account.
You are clear of the area. Cruise when you are ready.
Negative, Kestrel One. Not enough fuel for that leg. Fill up first.
Landing zone in sight. Bring her in nice and slow.

sounds.text: You dented the bucket. It will leak until the shop fixes it.
Too fast over the water. Slow down or you will tear the bucket.
That is the bucket. Hover low and slow over the lake and let it sink and fill.
Bucket is full. She is heavier now, so give her more collective.
Fireweed is blooming in the burn. It is always the first flower back after a fire.
The burnt woods are open again. All black for now, but it will come back.
Green shoots are coming up in the burn.
Hold H to let the water go. Drop low, and a little short. The water keeps moving as it falls.
Thank you, Kestrel One. Fit the bucket at the pad. The lake is your water.
Calling all pilots, calling all pilots. Smoke and flames reported in the forest. Kestrel One, can you take it?
Good work, Kestrel One. It is half out.
Understood. Call us back when you can. It will not wait forever.
We have lost those woods. The course is closed. Nobody was hurt.
That is the last of it. Fire is out. Great flying, Kestrel One.
Kestrel One, that fire is still burning, and it is growing.
From all of us at the park, thank you. The animals thank you too.
There is a breeze. Watch where the water drifts.
Wind is light today.
It is windy out there. The fire runs with the wind, so hit the downwind side first.

sounds.text: Calling all pilots. Avalanche on the ski hill. A skier is buried. Kestrel One, can you take it?
You have a signal. Follow the beeps. Faster means closer.
Thank you. They were last seen inside the circle on your map. Fly low and slow, and watch for an orange flare.
Kestrel One, park rangers here. A hiker is lost in the forest and it will be dark soon. Can you search for them?
It is getting dark, Kestrel One.
That is them! There is a clearing close by. Land there and they will walk over.
Calling all pilots. A car has gone off the road, and the driver is stuck on the slope below. Kestrel One, can you take it?
That is the rescue line. Fly smooth, and keep her under forty knots with people on it.
Lower the rescuer gently, right beside them, and hold her there.
Thank you, Kestrel One. Fit the rescue line at the pad. Your rescuer is waiting.
Easy! You are hurting them.
They are clipped on. Lift gently.
Safe and sound. Great work, Kestrel One.
Slow down! People on the line.
The ground team got there first. They are badly hurt and on their way to hospital.
They are hurt, but they will be all right. The paramedics have them.
They are badly hurt. The paramedics are taking them to hospital.
They are getting cold, Kestrel One. Hurry.
Understood. If you cannot get there, another crew will.
Hold her steady. The rescuer needs you still.
Another crew has taken that call, Kestrel One.
Wildfire season is here. Keep an eye out for smoke.
Winter is here. Watch the ski hill for avalanches.
Thanks, Kestrel One. Three crates are waiting by the pad. Bring them to the yard by the lodge.
Kestrel One, this is the lodge. Snow has shut the road and we are running low. Can you fly supplies up?
Crate is down. Thank you.
That is everything. The whole lodge thanks you, Kestrel One.
The lodge sent a snowcat in the end. They are still short of supplies.

Close enough to be useful. Thanks.

That is a long way from our numbers. Try more lines next time.
Did you see that? That one is rare. Lucky you.
Too low! You are scaring them off.
Thanks, Kestrel One. Fly straight lines across the square, and stay high enough not to scare them.
Shiny as new.
She is filthy, Kestrel One. A wash at the pad will fix that.

sounds.text: That is one. Again.
Not that time. Back to zero. You know how.
Good. Now beat my time through the corner. Three in a row.
Two. One more.
Brake at the first cone. Not before, not after.
Back on the gas sooner, and let the car run out wide.
Get closer to the inside cone. Use the whole road.
I heard the tyres. Brake a little earlier and keep it smooth.
Welcome to the track. Today is the most important corner skill there is: braking. Forget the course boards today and watch my cones.
You braked early. Good instinct, but this time I wanted you to feel it. That one still counts.
Let us see what happens when you leave it late. Keep your foot down and brake at the red board.
Three in a row. You have earned better brakes, and the next lesson is open.
That is it. Quiet tyres, clean line, and quicker too.
Now the right way. Brake hard at the first cone while the car is straight, turn in, touch the inside cone, and accelerate out wide past the third.
Back for more? Good. Practice is how the fast drivers got fast.

processing.normalization: FFmpeg loudnorm, TP -3, LRA 11; limiter .70 without auto-level

sounds.text: Lesson two: the racing line. Through linked corners, the fastest way is not the shortest.
First, stay in the middle of the road. Follow the markers.
Felt tight, didn't it? The middle of the road makes every bend sharper, so you have to go slower.
Now use the whole road. Start wide, touch each inside cone, and let the car run out wide between them.
Closer to the inside cone. Use every bit of road.
You turned in too early and ran out of road. Wait a moment longer, then turn.
Feel how straight that was? A wider line is a gentler curve, and a gentler curve is a faster one.
Now beat my time through the esses. Three in a row.
Three in a row. Better handling for your car, and the next lesson is open.
Lesson three: the gearbox. Today you change gear yourself. E is up, Q is down.
First, change up as soon as the needle passes the green mark.
Sluggish, wasn't it? An engine is weak at low revs. Changing up early drops it below where it pulls.
Now hold each gear until the lights come on, then change up. Change down while you brake, so you leave the corner in my gear.
That was the limiter. Change up when the lights come on, not after.
Too high a gear coming out. Change down while you brake.
Hear it pull out of the corner? That's the right gear.
Now beat my time, changing gear yourself. Three in a row.
Three in a row. More power for your car, and the next lesson is open.
Lesson four: snow. On summer tyres you have about half the grip you have on a dry road.
First, brake where you would on a dry road. The red board shows it.
Half the grip means about twice the road to stop. That's why you ran out of corner.
Now brake at the snow cone, gently. Do your braking before the ice, never on it. Then turn in smooth.
Earlier. On snow, start braking at the cone.
You braked on the ice. Brake before it, roll across it, then turn.
Turn in more gently. Sudden steering on snow slides the front.
Smooth and early. That's how you drive on snow.
Now beat my time, three in a row, on summer tyres.
Same corner, now on winter tyres. Feel the difference.
Winter tyres use softer rubber that stays grippy in the cold, and deep cuts that bite into the snow.
That's every driving lesson I have for now. Better tyres for your car. Well driven.
Hear that screech? Your tyres slid past their best grip, so the car could not steer or stop as well. You got away with it here. On snow you won't.
That's where a slide takes you. Brake at the first cone, and keep it clean.
